messages:
maria: Quick question — compliance wants a crisp definition of custody boundaries for customer-managed keys (HSM-backed) in Redwood Private. They also want proposed RBAC changes, audit log shape + retention, and an incident triage flow if a key compromise is suspected. Can we sketch this in thread form?

anil: Sure. Can you confirm the deployment variants we need to cover? (VPC-managed KMS, on-prem HSM appliance, cloud KMS with BYOK import)

maria: Yep exactly those three. Also note: customer may require that Redwood never stores plaintext key material and that HSM PKCS11 exports are disabled.

lucy: Important compliance constraints: SOC2 + ISO27001 baseline, some customers asking for FIPS 140-2 Level 3 attestation and EU data residency. For on-prem HSMs, we need proof of tamper-resistance and chain-of-custody docs.

dmitri: High level custody boundaries I propose: 1) VPC-managed KMS (customer-managed keys): root key material lives in cloud KMS under customer project/account; Redwood gets only wrapped keys or data keys via secure RPC, no unwrap capability persisted. 2) On-prem HSM: key material never leaves customer network; Redwood agents request signing operations via mutually authenticated mTLS and only exchange operation tokens. 3) BYOK import to Redwood-managed HSM: allowed only if customer signs an escrow/escrow-approval and we provide attestation that master key is sealed — but prefer to avoid unless contractually required.

maria: That sounds good. For RBAC, can we be explicit? A draft: create three new roles scoped to customer X: `hsm_admin` (can configure HSM integr, rotate wrapping key), `hsm_operator` (can trigger key ops like rotate/revoke, but cannot export), `key_audit_reader` (read-only access to audit events).

anil: +1. Minimal principle: no single human should have both `hsm_admin` and `key_audit_reader` in sensitive accounts. Also require MFA + timebound sessions for `hsm_admin` (e.g., 1h), and all admin actions require an approval ticket in our ticketing system.

lucy: Audit log shape suggestion (keeps PII out):
```
{
  "event_ts": "ISO8601",
  "actor": "redwood:user|service-account",
  "actor_id": "<id>",
  "action": "unwrap|wrap|sign|import|rotate|revoke|config_change",
  "key_id": "arn-like-or-uuid",
  "hsm_endpoint": "hostname-or-connector-id",
  "success": true|false,
  "request_id": "uuid",
  "reason": "optional free text",
  "audit_hash": "sha256 of record for tamper-evidence"
}
```
Retention: baseline 2 years for customer-facing audit records (some customers require 7 years). Internal debug logs (no key material) 90 days. All logs must be write-once and append-only in storage with immutable retention policy.

dmitri: For KMS integration options: prefer native cloud KMS via IAM roles (least code). For on-prem appliances use KMIP or PKCS11 with an agent that proxies ops over mTLS and authenticated sessions. For import flows, require HSM attestation and require `no_export` policy bit.

ops-bot: NOTE: New RBAC roles will trigger policy lint checks. Run `tools/policy-check --roles hsm_admin,hsm_operator` after PR.

maria: Vulnerability triage: if a vulnerability is found in the HSM agent or connector we should: 1) classify severity (CVSS + exploitability), 2) if remote code exec affecting key material -> treat as high/incident, 3) rotate wrapping keys ASAP and roll short-lived data keys, 4) notify impacted customers with recommended mitigations, 5) convene incident guild.

sre-oncall: Oncall ops note: For suspected compromise we need a kill-switch path that does not rely on single operator (two-person approval). That should be callable via console API with audit recording. Also prepare pre-generated emergency rotation manifests per customer.

anil: Incident playbook sketch:
- DECLARE: severity and customer impact matrix
- CONTAIN: disable HSM connector ingress, revoke service certs, block agent from accepting new ops
- ERADICATE: rotate wrapping key(s), re-encrypt persisted blobs with new key material or issue forced rewrap request to customer KMS
- RECOVER: staged rollout of patched agent, smoke tests for sign/unwrap ops, re-enable connectors
- REVIEW: postmortem, evidence archive, and attestation letter to customers for legal/compliance

lucy: Compliance notes: customers in scope for regulated data will require contract-level SLAs and indemnities for key compromise; many require proof of key provenance and that we do not, ever, store unwrapped customer keys. Also ensure Data Processing Agreements mention key custody model.

maria: One more practical thing — logging access: key_audit_reader must be pushed to a separate log-viewer with IP allowlist and client's security contact must be recorded. Also escalate if any admin action occurs outside business hours.

dmitri: I'll draft an RBAC JSON snippet for the repo and a sample audit retention policy RFC. Quick sample policy (very rough):
```json
{
  "roles": [
    {"name": "hsm_admin", "perms": ["config:modify","key:rotate"], "session_ttl": 3600},
    {"name": "hsm_operator", "perms": ["key:rotate","key:revoke","op:request"], "session_ttl": 7200},
    {"name": "key_audit_reader", "perms": ["audit:read"], "session_ttl": 86400}
  ]
}
```

maria: Great. Can you land a short RFC? Call it "HSM custody & BYOK boundaries" and include: custody diagrams, RBAC snippet, audit schema, incident playbook, and integration checklist (KMIP/PKCS11/cloud). I'll loop in Legal + Sales for contract language.

anil: I'll own the RFC draft. tagging @compliance-bot for any automatic checklist gaps.

compliance-bot: ACTION: created checklist ticket CHK-4821 for: attestation docs, retention opt-ins, contract clause templates, and customer notification templates.

maria: Thanks all — tagging for follow-ups: @lucy please add compliance risks, @dmitri please prod the eng docs PR. We'll review in Thursday security sync. :thumbsup:
